candidates.exact_span: 1. Pollutant limits - The concentration of the pollutants in the municipal sewage sludge is at or below the values listed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the compliance comparison direction (at or below) for Table 3 pollutant concentrations; a different reading of whether this is an enforceable numeric limit versus descriptive preamble would change whether reported measurements are evaluated for exceedance.

candidates.exact_span: All bulk sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, a reclamation site, or lawn or home garden shall be treated by the Class A pathogen reduction requirements as defined above in Element I, Section I.B.3. All bagged sewage sludge must be treated by Class A pathogen reduction requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditions pathogen-control obligations on sludge application type (bulk vs. bagged and land-use categories); different interpretations of which practices trigger Class A treatment would change whether related monitoring or documentation was required, and how missing pathogen evidence should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall develop the following information and shall retain the information for five years. The sludge documents will be retained on site at the same location as other NPDES records.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes recordkeeping obligations and retention location/duration that define what evidence should exist for sludge compliance; interpretation affects whether absent records indicate missing required evidence or an unresolved applicability state.

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 3 and the applicable pollutant concentration criteria listed in Table 3.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires retention of measured concentrations alongside applicable Table 3 criteria; affects which pollutants must be documented, what limit values are paired with measurements for Purpose A, and whether missing records represent inadequate evidence for required monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: A certification statement that all applicable requirements (specifically listed) have been met, and that the permittee understands that there are significant penalties for false certification including fine and imprisonment. See 503.17(a)(1)(ii) or 503.17(a)(3)(i)(B), whichever applies to the permittees sludge treatment activities.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a certification obligation whose applicability depends on which 503.17 provision applies to the permittee's sludge treatment activities; different interpretations of 'specifically listed' requirements or the cross-reference would change evaluated monitoring/documentation obligations and how missing certification is categorized.

candidates.exact_span: A description of how the Class A pathogen reduction requirements are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires documented evidence of pathogen reduction compliance; interpretation of whether this documentation obligation is independently required affects monitoring/recordkeeping applicability and classification of absent pathogen evidence.

candidates.exact_span: A description of how the vector attraction reduction requirements are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires documented evidence of vector attraction reduction; whether this obligation is operative for a given practice affects evaluated requirements and how missing documentation is treated under missing-evidence semantics.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall report annually on the DMR the following information:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes an annual DMR reporting obligation; interpretation of timing and scope determines which monitoring periods in FY2025 require reported results and how absent DMR entries are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Pollutant Table 3 appropriate for permittee's land application practices.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Table 3 pollutants must be reported depends on the permittee's land application practices; different interpretations of 'appropriate' would change which limits and measurements are in scope for numeric comparison, which monitoring was required, and whether missing data is conditional or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 1, Section I.C. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reporting obligation incorporates monitoring frequency from an external permit element; interpretation of which Section I.C. frequency applies to the permittee determines expected monitoring intervals and whether absent results reflect non-required periods versus missing evidence.

Requires TCLP pass/fail reporting rather than a numeric concentration; interpretation affects whether compliance is evaluated as a binary limit (Purpose A), whether TCLP monitoring was required (Purpose B), and how non-numeric or missing TCLP results are classified (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 1 (defined as a monthly average) found in Element 1, Section I. In addition, the applicable pollutant concentration criteria listed in Table 3 should be included on the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Pairs reported monthly-average Table 1 measurements with Table 3 criteria on the DMR; interpretation of which Table 1 pollutants apply, what 'monthly average' means for a monitoring period, and whether criteria 'should be included' is mandatory affects limit applicability, monitoring obligations, and treatment of incomplete DMR data.
